Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE BIVAHENC St6NATL•2E: OATE• rlMF' CORT20L DILG Legal Opinion No. 4 s, 2012 IJAN 2 5 2012 MAYOR HERMINIGILDO M. BETONIO Ill Acting Mayor, Municipality of Pio V. Cruz Province of Masbate Dear Mayor Betonio Ill: This has reference to your letters dated IO January 2012 and 22 January 2012 wherein you raised several issues for clarification and a request for opinion on the validity of your assumption to office. For ease of reference, we quote your queries: I. 2. 3. 4. Is my assumption into office as Acting Municipal Mayor thru rule of succession effective and inoperative? I took my Oath of Office as Acting Municipaly Mayor , this Municipality, before DILG Secretary Hon. Jesse M Robredo last December 28, 2011, is this legal? If the Sangguniang Bayan fails to enact a resolution, upon request of the undersigned, regarding endorsement to the official depository bank (Development Bank of the Philippines[DBP] of Pio V. Corpus, Masbate for my official transaction and specimen signature application, it will surely hamper the financial transactions of the LGU, xxx. Who will be responsible/liable for all these deficiencies? The Sangguniang Bayan during their regular section expressly and vehemently denied the veracity and authenticity of 'the Oath of Office of the undersigned Acting Municipal Mayor and did not officially accept a copy thereof. Is their action lawful?" Our Comments: On the First and Second Issues: The first issue had already been clarified in our letter dated 29 December 2011 addressed to Gov. Seachon-Lanete wherein we cited the case of "Re: Irrevocable Resignation of Emmanuel G. Mifion, 18 October 2000' In our jurisdiction, acceptance is necessary for resignation of a public officer to be operative and effective. Without acceptance, resignation is nothing and the officer remains in office. Resignation to be effective must be accepted by competent authority, either in terms or by something tantamount to an acceptance, such as the appointment of the successor. A public officer cannot abandon his office before his resignation is accepted, otherwise the officer is subject to the penal provisions of Article 238 of the Revised Penal Code. The final or conclusive act of a resignation's acceptance is the notice of acceptance. The incumbent official would not be in a position to determine the acceptance of his resignation unless he had been duly notified therefor. (Republic of the Philippines vs Winston T. Singun, GR. No. 149356, 14 March 2008)

However, even in the absence of acceptance by a competent authority, the irrevocable resignation submitted by then Mayor Diomedes Amaroto Sr. tendered on 07 December 2011 and his conspicuous absence since then showed a clear intent to relinquish the office as he voluntarily did so. Citing the same case of Miöon, the Supreme Court held that the absence of acceptance, which is an indispensable requirement, made Miäon's resignation incomplete and ineffective. Notwithstanding, the Court ruled that Miäon was deemed to have relinquished his office through NON-USE, citing the case of Sangguniang Bayan of San Andres, Catanduanes vs. Court of Appeals, et al., G.R. No. 118883, January 16, 1998: "Even if the resignation is not valid for absence of an acceptance by the proper authority, a public officer may be deemed to have relinquished his office due to his voluntary abandonment of said post. "xx x. "Abandonment of an office has been defined as the voluntary relinquishment of an office by the holder, with the intention of terminating his position and control thereof. Indeed, abandonment of office is a species of resignation; while resignation in general is a formal relinquishment through non-user. Non-user refers to a neglect to use a privilege or a right (Cyclopedic Law Dictionary, 3rd ed.) or to exercise an easement or an office (Black's Law Dictionary, 6th ed.). " On the issue of your having taken an Oath before the Secretary of this Department to assume and perform the functions and responsibilities of the Office of the Mayor in an acting capacity, such act is legal. At the time of your assumption to office on 28 December 2011, the resignation of then Mayor Amaroto had not been accepted by Gov. Lanete, the competent and proper authority to accept said resignation. The letter dated 29 December 2011 from DILG Usec. Austere Panadero addressed to Gov. Lanete was made in response to Mayor Amaroto's query, seeking an opinion on the refusal by Gov. Lanete of Mayor Amaroto's resignation, and clearly showed due deference to Gov. Lanete's right to exercise her prerogative to act on Mayor Amaroto's irrevocable resignation pursuant to Section 82(a)(2) of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Applying the ruling on the Miäon case, the Office of the Municipal Mayor of Pio V. Cruz is rendered vacant arising from the voluntary relinquishment by the former Mayor Amaroto, and such act caused a permanent vacancy in the said office. As a legal consequence, the Vice Mayor shall become the Mayor applying the rule of succession under Section 44 (a) of RA 7160. On the Third and Fourth Issues: Your current dilemma is the repeated refusal by the Sangguniang Bayan of Pio V. Cruz to enact appropriate resolution authorizing the former to represent the Municipality of Pio V. Cruz in its dealings and transactions with respect to the accounts of the said LGU. Without the resolution, you cannot make any official transaction with the bank, hampering the financial transactions of the LGU, primarily the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits to officials and employees of the LGU, among others.

The Sangguniang Bayan of Pio V. Cruz is legally bound to recognize your authority as Acting Mayor Betonio considering your valid assumption to said Office. Thus, as Acting Mayor, you may lawfully assume and perform the functions of the Office of the Municipal Mayor. Further, it may be noted that the designation in an acting capacity entails not only the exercise of the ministerial functions attached to the position but also the exercise of discretion. (In Re: Vitriolo, Julito D., CSC Resolution No. 000778, 24 March 2000) Hence, the obstinate refusal by the local sanggunian may give rise to possible legal actions. We hope the foregoing sufficiently clarified your queries. Very truly yours, J SUS B Director Ill LS:55/06 o
